item.title: To the Point! Supply Chain Management Design
item.content:encoded:
Matthias Klumpp,

Medo Pournader,

Carl Marcus Wallenburg,

Stan Fawcett,

Mike Knemeyer,

This special issue calls for original, impactful research on supply chain management that addresses contemporary business challenges. The work should demonstrate practical relevance to decision-makers while advancing theory, combining rigor with accessibility for both academics and practitioners. Research must be based on recent empirical data and present findings that are timely, thought-provoking, and clearly communicated.

The journal seeks papers examining how organizations can design efficient supply chain systems and develop distinctive capabilities to navigate dynamic markets. Topics include supply chain process innovation, managing sustainability and risk trade-offs, reconfiguring global operations amid geopolitical pressures, developing enabling policies, fostering cross-organizational collaboration, and leveraging emerging technologies like AI to gain competitive advantage.

Appel publié par Journal of Business Logistics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Designing supply chain processes and systems for competitive success
  • Sustainability, risk, and operational excellence connections
  • Global supply chain footprint redesign
  • Public policy for supply chain transformation
  • Value creation across organizational boundaries
  • Technology and AI for supply chain capabilities
  • Innovation for solving complex problems

Timeline

  • December 31, 2026: Abstract submission deadline
  • January 15, 2027: Feedback on abstracts
  • April 1, 2027: Full paper submission window opens
  • April 30, 2027: Full paper submission window closes

item.title: Past Accomplishments and Future Challenges within Supply Chain Management Research
item.content:encoded:
Jessica L. Darby, Auburn University

Rebekah (Bekki) Brau, Brigham Young University

David J. Ketchen, Auburn University

This annual special issue invites authors to submit proposals for integrative literature reviews of important supply chain management research streams. The special issue aims to synthesize current knowledge and provide direction for future development in the field. Rather than submitting full papers, authors propose a review project that outlines how they will examine and synthesize a focused area of SCM scholarship.

Proposals are evaluated on their significance, feasibility, potential breadth of interest, clarity, and contribution to future research directions. The review should address a notable gap in existing literature or provide substantial new perspective beyond prior reviews. The guest editors emphasize that proposals must be carefully crafted and authors should seek colleague feedback before submission, as rough drafts will not be pre-screened.

Appel publié par Journal of Business Logistics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Integrative reviews of supply chain management research that focus on a specific topic or apply a particular theory across different topics
  • Research streams in supply chain management that require scholarly review
  • Significant SCM research areas with limited recent published reviews or novel contributions beyond existing reviews
  • Supply chain management topics of broad interest across specialty areas and neighboring fields
